description:
FILED s446m (Opus, agent M) as the DESIGNED-BUT-NOT-SHIPPED half of #73, so it is not re-derived: the per-CLASS method cache (perl's own shape) is the only remaining lever on INHERITED dispatch, and its blocker is INVALIDATION, not the cache.  After s446m the inherited loop is 0.71 s / 2M calls vs 0.21 s for the same call written as a plain sub call (3.4x), and the profile is FIND-SYMBOL: one per class per call up the @ISA chain, each hashing the "pl-NAME" string.  A cache keyed by (package, sub-name) -> function with a global generation counter (perl's PL_sub_generation / mro_method_changed_in) removes all of them.  The generation must be bumped at EVERY mutation point: a sub definition, a glob assignment (*Foo::bar = sub {...}), and ANY WRITE TO ANY @ISA -- push, list assign, splice, element set, `local @ISA`, and a write through a reference.  The first two are single sites; the third is the blocker, because @ISA in PCL is an ordinary array box with no magic, so there is no one place a write passes through.  perl solves it by making @ISA magical.  The PCL shape would be the box magic hook (reference_box_magic_hook): mark the @isa array box at package-creation time and have the array writers bump the generation when they see the mark.  A missed mutation point = a stale cache = silently dispatching to the wrong method, the worst failure mode in this codebase -- so this needs the marker first, a die-loud audit of every array write path, and the full sweep + companion legs. DO NOT ship it as "just a hash table".

s445 (Fable): SCHEDULED POST-v0.1 -- the @ISA-write invalidation blocker is a magic-hook design question (same era as boxed aggregates); inherited dispatch stays at ~3.4x a plain sub call until then, documented as the ceiling in faster-codegen-suggestions.md §7.
RE-MEASURED s454ac (Opus, round 12 perf agent, 2026-08-30) -- the lag is
STILL THERE and the ordering is unchanged; measurement only, NOT
implemented, because the honest bar (the @ISA-write invalidation marker +
the die-loud audit of every array write path + full sweep + companion legs)
is session-sized on its own and this session's budget went to #680.

The numbers (2M calls, exec = t(N=2M) - t(N=0) via runpcl, best-of-5
minimum; taken while sibling round-12 agents loaded the box at ~7-9, so
ABSOLUTES are inflated ~30-100% -- the RATIOS are the finding):

    shape                          perl        pcl
    inherited $o->v() via @ISA     0.3144 s    0.9843 s
    monomorphic $o->v()            0.1993 s    0.4699 s
    same call as B::v($o)          0.1633 s    0.1877 s

    inherited / plain-sub (PCL)  = 5.2x   (s446m quiet-machine: 3.5x)
    inherited / monomorphic      = 2.1x   -- the @ISA walk pays ~0.26 us
                                             per call over the own-package
                                             fast path
    monomorphic vs perl          = 2.4x   (s446m: 2.62x -- consistent)

So the per-CLASS cache would still fire on inherited dispatch, and the
blocker remains exactly as filed: invalidation on @ISA writes needs the box
magic hook first.  Probe shapes preserved in the launcher scratchpad
recipe: m-inh.pl / m-mono.pl / m-sub.pl (packages B2/C2, C3, B4; the loop
is `for (1..$n) { $s += $o->v() }` with N from env).


=== OWN-CLASS HALF DONE (s473s, 2026-09-08) — the INHERITED half is still this task ===

THE MEASUREMENT FIRST (sb-sprof, :cpu, 1 ms, the `methret` bench program at
N = 20 M, 2970 samples, load 4.2 — the RATIOS are the finding).  Where
methret's 133 ns per call go, by self time, grouped:

    PROLOGUE (p-method-call before the apply)              58.7 %
      %pcl-own-method                                      23.0 %
        of which FIND-SYMBOL (%find-symbol/%lookup-symbol/  16.6 %
          calc-symbol-name-hash/string=*)
        of which %pcl-find-package (the s446m stash memo)    2.0 %
      p-method-call self (the let*, the type tests, apply) 11.7 %
      %pcl-normalize-class-name                             9.2 %
        of which the two generic (string= c "…")            6.5 %
      %pcl-invocant-class -> p-get-class -> gethash          6.8 %
        :__class__ on the object's own hash
      %pcl-cl-sub-name (memoized "pl-bump")                  2.7 %
      unbox (the method arg, the invocant)                  ~2.2 %
      (position #\: method-name)                             1.1 %
      to-string                                              0.7 %
    CALLEE (pl-bump)                                       36.2 %
      the $self->{v} hash read (p-gethash + -deref)         19.3 %
      the lambda's own body, %p-args-need-flatten, +        16.9 %
    LOOP (p-foreach-range-raw, p-incf-raw, p-scalar-ctx)     4.0 %

    ALLOCATION: methret 48.0 bytes/iteration; subret 48.0 bytes/iteration --
    IDENTICAL.  The dispatch prologue allocates NOTHING (methret's call site
    passes no arguments, so the &rest list is NIL), which is why the
    fixed-arity `p-method-call-N` lever would buy nothing on this row.

So the LOOKUP dominates, and the own-class half of this task is what removes
it.  SHIPPED s473s: a two-level EQUAL table (class name as the invocant
spells it -> method name as the call site spells it -> the SYMBOL), probed
before the normalisation, the `pl-NAME` build and the colon scan.

**IT NEEDED NO GENERATION COUNTER, and that is the finding this task should
carry forward.**  Storing the SYMBOL rather than the FUNCTION makes the cache
immune to every redefinition path by construction: `p-sub`, `*Foo::bar = sub
{…}`, `*Foo::bar = \&baz`, a string-eval'd sub and `local *Foo::bar` (entry
AND restore) all write through `(setf (symbol-function …))` /
`(setf (fdefinition …))` on the SAME symbol, and every removal path
(`undef &Foo::bar`) calls `fmakunbound`, which the entry's `fboundp` re-test
sees.  Nothing in the runtime uninterns a symbol or changes its home package.
The audit-every-mutation-site design this task described is therefore NOT what
was built, and should not be built for the own half.

MEASURED (base c2016433, interleaved 3-column A/B, byte-identical control):
methret -27.5 % (control +1.4 %), ovlsub -5.8 %, json-rt -4.8 %, moo-objs
-0.9 % (-5.8 % on an earlier base), and the PURE-INHERITED shape 0.0 %.

WHAT IS LEFT — THE INHERITED HALF, still blocked exactly as filed.  An own
MISS is not cached (a method defined later would be masked, and the resolved
INHERITED method depends on @ISA, whose writes PCL cannot see).  Its cost,
measured on the same instrument: a pure-inherited `$o->bump` through one @ISA
level is 274 ns vs 137 ns monomorphic (2.0x), and the monomorphic side is now
99 ns, so the inherited/own ratio is 2.8x.  The blocker is unchanged: @ISA is
an ordinary array box with no magic, so there is no one place a write passes
through -- the box magic hook (reference_box_magic_hook) marking the @ISA
array at package-creation time, plus a die-loud audit of every array write
path, is still the precondition.

NOTE for whoever takes it: because the own half caches the SYMBOL, an
inherited-half cache can use the SAME table and the SAME fboundp re-test for
redefinition; the ONLY thing it must add is @ISA-write invalidation.  That is
a strictly smaller job than this task's original description assumed.



=== s473s (2026-09-08): the OWN-CLASS half is SHIPPED; this task is now the INHERITED half only ===

`p-method-call` caches `(class name as the invocant spells it, method name as
the call site spells it) -> the SYMBOL` and probes it before
`%pcl-normalize-class-name`, the `pl-NAME` build and the colon scan.  Measured:
`methret` **-27.5 %**, `ovlsub` -5.8 %, `json-rt` -4.8 %, `methinh` 0.0 %
(pure inherited dispatch pays the failed probe and gains nothing, and must not
regress).  Guard `Pl/t/method-cache-01.t`; ir-spec §7.3 rewritten, since it
still said "nothing about the resolution is cached".

THE FINDING THAT MAKES THE REMAINING HALF SMALLER: **no generation counter is
needed for an own-class HIT.**  The cached value is the SYMBOL, not the
function, so every path that (re)defines a Perl sub — `p-sub`, `*Foo::bar =
sub {…}`, `*Foo::bar = \&baz`, a string-eval'd sub, `local *Foo::bar` and its
restore — writes through `(setf (symbol-function …))` on that same symbol and
the entry answers with the new definition for free; every path that removes one
calls `fmakunbound`, which the entry's own `fboundp` test sees, declining to
the slow path.  Nothing uninterns a symbol or changes its home package.  So the
whole `PL_sub_generation` apparatus this task was designed around is unneeded
for the own half.

WHAT IS LEFT HERE, unchanged: an own MISS is never stored, so an inherited call
still re-walks `@ISA` on every call and an `@ISA` edit between two calls is
visible on the second (asserted by the guard).  Caching that answer DOES need
the `@ISA`-write invalidation marker — the box magic hook — exactly as filed.
